mainTopic: Spices on coals and מוליד ריחא, the גדי מקולס, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's leniencies with the dispute over דבר שאינו מתכוין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ruling: spices may not be sprinkled on coals on יום טוב, but they may go on a hot piece of earthenware (חרס). רבה forbids even that, because it creates a new scent (מוליד ריחא), while רבא permits spices even directly on coals, comparing it to roasting meat on coals. A story follows about רב גביהא's ruling that קיטורא is permitted. אמימר challenges that ruling, and רב אשי defends it as burning incense, which is allowed just like meat on coals. Next the גמרא explains רבן גמליאל's leniency of the גדי מקולס, and tells how the חכמים objected when תודוס of Rome had people eat a whole roasted kid on פסח night, because it looked like קדשים. A new משנה then lists three things רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid, including combing an animal on יום טוב. The גמרא explains that the cow called 'his' was really his neighbor's. It then shows that the three opinions on combing depend on whether an unintended forbidden result (דבר שאינו מתכוין) is allowed. רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון that it is permitted.

steps.title: Spices on hot earthenware are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that began on the previous amud ends: sprinkling spices on a hot piece of earthenware (חרס) is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on a hot piece of earthenware, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a ruling that started on the previous amud. That ruling forbade putting spices directly on coals on יום טוב, and this line says that putting them on a hot piece of earthenware is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spices sprinkled on burning coals can put out part of the fire, which is כיבוי. A hot piece of earthenware is not burning, so there is nothing to put out and the problem disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece of earthenware or pottery (here, a heated shard)

phrases.english: On top of an earthenware shard — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This ends the earlier ruling, which forbade putting spices on coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling on the previous amud boundary (coals forbidden, earthenware permitted).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices may be placed on a hot earthenware shard on יום טוב, since there is no burning fire to extinguish.

steps.title: רבה forbids even earthenware because it creates a new scent
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees and forbids spices even on hot earthenware, because doing so creates a new scent (מוליד ריחא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Even on earthenware it is forbidden, because he creates a scent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a stricter opinion. He forbids putting spices even on the hot shard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה adds a new reason to forbid that has nothing to do with fire. Making a new smell soak into an object counts as creating something new (מוליד), and that is not allowed on יום טוב. So even the 'safe' earthenware option is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה's reason is not about fire at all. Even with zero risk of extinguishing, he forbids it because a new scent is created.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
On top of earthenware it is also forbidden,
because he is creating a scent.
phrases.notes: The scent is absorbed into the shard, which counts as making something new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 1's permission for earthenware.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices on hot earthenware are forbidden on יום טוב because of מוליד ריחא.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף forbid perfuming silk clothes
steps.stepSummary: A parallel ruling from רבה and רב יוסף: turning a cup of perfume over onto silk clothes on יום טוב is forbidden because it creates a scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: Turning a cup over onto silk garments on a Festival is forbidden. What is the reason? Because he creates a scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling built on the same principle of מוליד ריחא. This shows that the idea is not a one-time opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a cup of perfume turned over onto silk so the cloth soaks up the smell. The silk did not smell before and now it does, so a new scent has been made. This is the same reasoning רבה used for the earthenware.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both said:

phrases.aramaic: סַחוֹפֵי כָּסָא אַשִּׁירָאֵי בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Overturning a cup (of perfume) onto silk garments on a Festival — forbidden,
What is the reason? Because he creates a scent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case that supports the מוליד ריחא principle from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Perfuming silk clothes on יום טוב is forbidden because a new scent is created in them.

steps.title: Challenge: crushing or snipping a fragrant twig is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why perfuming clothes is different from the permitted acts of crushing or snipping a fragrant twig to smell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from 'one may crush it and smell it, and snip it and smell it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the מוליד ריחא principle using a known teaching that allows releasing scent from fragrant wood on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you crush or snip a fragrant twig, more smell comes out, so it looks like you are 'making' scent too. If that is allowed, why should perfuming silk or earthenware be forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: he crushes it (rubs it between his fingers)

phrases.english: And how is it different from 'he may crush it and smell it'
'and snip it and smell it'?
phrases.notes: Quoting an earlier teaching about fragrant wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle of steps 2-3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that creating scent (מוליד ריחא) is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Crushing or snipping fragrant wood also produces more scent, yet it is permitted. So scent production should not be forbidden.

steps.title: Adding to an existing scent vs. creating a new one
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the fragrant twig already has its smell and crushing only makes it stronger. Perfuming silk puts a smell where there was none.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the scent is there anyway, and he is only adding scent. Here, he is creating a scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by drawing a line between strengthening a smell and making a brand-new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twig already smells, so crushing it only adds to what exists (אוסופי). Silk or earthenware has no smell of its own, so perfuming it brings a new scent into being (אולודי). Only the second counts as מוליד and is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Strengthening a scent that already exists is permitted. Creating a new scent in an object (מוליד ריחא) is forbidden, according to רבה and רב יוסף.

phrases.english: There — the scent is there in any case,
and he is only adding more scent.
Here — he is creating a new scent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any release of scent should count as creating scent, so crushing a twig would be the same as perfuming silk.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only bringing a scent into an object that had none is מוליד. Strengthening an existing scent is permitted.

steps.title: רבא permits spices even directly on coals
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes the lenient position: spices may be put even directly on coals, just as meat may be roasted on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even on a coal it is permitted, just as with meat on coals.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third opinion that is the most lenient of all. He permits even the case that was first forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting meat on coals is allowed on יום טוב even though dripping fat puts out some of the coals. רבא says spices on coals are the same: the small extinguishing is not a problem. Because he permits even coals, he clearly does not forbid earthenware for מוליד ריחא either.

keyTerms.meaning: just like, the same as (comparison formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: The comparison 'meat on coals' comes back in Steps 9 and 11, where רב אשי uses it to answer אמימר's challenge to רב גביהא.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: עַל גַּבֵּי גַּחֶלֶת נָמֵי מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: Rava said: On top of a coal it is also permitted,
just as it is with meat on coals.
phrases.notes: Roasting meat on coals is permitted even though fat drips and extinguishes some coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a lenient opinion against both the original ruling (coals forbidden) and רבה (earthenware forbidden).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spices may be placed even directly on coals on יום טוב, like roasting meat on coals.

steps.title: רב גביהא teaches that קיטורא is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהא of בי כתיל publicly taught at the ראש גלותא's house that קיטורא is permitted on יום טוב, without explaining the word.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהא מבי כתיל expounded at the entrance of the ריש גלותא's house: קיטורא is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins with a short public teaching. The unclear word sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קיטורא can mean 'tying' (קשירה) or 'burning incense' (קטורת). Because רב גביהא did not say which one he meant, the next step asks him.

keyTerms.meaning: the Exilarch, leader of the Babylonian Jewish community
an unclear word: tying, or burning incense

phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Katil expounded
at the entrance of the Exilarch's house:
'Ketura' is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a related story about incense on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קיטורא is permitted on יום טוב (meaning still unclear).

steps.title: אמימר: both meanings of קיטורא should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אמימר asks what קיטורא means, and argues that both possible meanings should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said to him: What is קיטורא? If it means tying by hand, that is a craftsman's work. And if it means burning incense, it is forbidden, because he extinguishes!
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר challenges רב גביהא's ruling. He shows that each way of reading the word leads to a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קיטורא means tying fancy knots, that is skilled craftsman's work (מעשה אומן) and is forbidden on יום טוב. If it means sprinkling incense on coals, that puts out some of the coals (מכבה). Either way the ruling seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: to make smoke, to burn incense

phrases.english: Ameimar said to him: What is 'ketura'?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קִטּוּרָא בִּידֵי — מַעֲשֵׂה אוּמָּן הוּא,
phrases.english: If it means tying by hand — that is a craftsman's work,
and if it means burning incense — it is forbidden,
because he is extinguishing!
phrases.notes: The spice powder puts out part of the coals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 7 by testing both possible meanings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גביהא's ruling that קיטורא is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible meanings are forbidden: tying is מעשה אומן, and burning incense causes כיבוי.

steps.title: רב אשי: it means burning incense, like meat on coals
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that קיטורא really does mean burning incense, and it is permitted just like roasting meat on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Actually it means burning incense, just as with meat on coals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רב גביהא's ruling. He accepts the 'incense' meaning and rejects the extinguishing objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי uses the same comparison רבא used. Meat may be roasted on coals even though it puts out some of them, so incense on coals is permitted too. The worry about כיבוי does not make it forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא and רב אשי, spices or incense may be put on coals on יום טוב, just as meat may be roasted on coals. The small amount of extinguishing does not forbid it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם לְעַשֵּׁן,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Actually, it means burning incense,
just as it is with meat on coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם לְעַשֵּׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אמימר's challenge in step 8, using the same comparison as רבא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an accepted case (מידי דהוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense would be forbidden because it extinguishes coals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Burning incense is permitted, just like roasting meat on coals, even though some coals are extinguished.

steps.title: Second version: אמימר challenges the meaning of קיטורא
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the story, אמימר asks what קיטורא means. He argues that both possible meanings should be forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the story went like this: אמימר said to him, 'What does קיטורא mean? If it means tying knots by hand, that is skilled craftsman's work. If it means making smoke with incense, that is forbidden, because he creates a new smell!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the story about רב גביהא's ruling. Here אמימר again attacks the ruling by showing that both meanings of קיטורא seem forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר sets up a trap with two options. Tying decorative knots is skilled work (מעשה אומן), which is not allowed. In this version, burning incense is attacked for creating a new smell (מוליד ריחא), like רבה's reasoning earlier, and not for extinguishing coals as in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some say'; introduces a second version of a story or ruling
The work of a skilled craftsman

steps.confusionAlert: This is a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the challenge in Step 8, and the reason is different. In Step 8, אמימר objects to burning incense because it extinguishes coals (מכבה). Here he objects because it creates a new smell (מוליד ריחא). רב אשי's answer in the next step also changes: he says he taught the ruling himself, in the name of a great man.

phrases.english: Some say (a different version):
Ameimar said to him:
What is 'ketura'?
phrases.notes: The word is ambiguous: it could mean tying knots or burning incense.

phrases.english: If it means tying by hand,
that is the work of a craftsman.
If it means to make smoke (burn incense),
it is forbidden, since he creates a smell!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַמֵּימָר: מַאי ״קִטּוּרָא״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the challenge of Step 8 as a second version of the same story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גביהא's public ruling that קיטורא is permitted on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible meanings fail: knot-tying is skilled craftsmanship, and incense-burning creates a new smell.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second version changes who stands behind the lenient answer, as the next step shows.

steps.title: רב אשי claims he taught the ruling in the name of a great teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that he himself told this ruling to רב גביהא, in the name of a great man (רבא). קיטורא means burning incense, and it is permitted just like putting meat on coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'I am the one who told it to him, and I told it to him in the name of a great man. It really does mean making smoke with incense, and it is just like putting meat on coals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He reveals that the ruling actually came from him, quoting a great teacher. He explains that it is about burning incense, which is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב גביהא was only repeating what רב אשי told him, and רב אשי was quoting a 'great man,' which is רבא. This ties the ruling to רבא's position from Step 6: putting spices on coals is like roasting meat on coals. Just as meat on coals is allowed even though it gives off a smell, incense on coals is allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man (here referring to רבא)
'Actually' / 'really'; keeps the original meaning despite the challenge

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way. קיטורא means burning incense, and it is permitted on יום טוב, just like roasting meat on coals, following רבא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said it to him,
and I said it to him in the name of a great man:
actually, it means making smoke,
and it is just like meat on coals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲנָא אַמְרִיתַהּ נִהֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אמימר's challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one horn of the dilemma (burning incense) and defends it with an analogy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning incense should be forbidden because it creates a new smell.
steps.terutzMaskana: Burning incense is like roasting meat on coals, which is permitted, so incense is permitted too.

steps.title: תודוס of Rome and the custom of a whole roasted kid on פסח night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about making a גדי מקולס. It then brings a ברייתא: תודוס of Rome led the Roman Jews to eat a whole roasted kid on פסח night, and the חכמים warned him that only his status saved him from נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And we may make a whole roasted kid.' A ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: תודוס of Rome led the Jews of Rome to eat a whole roasted kid on פסח nights. The חכמים sent him a message: 'If you were not תודוס, we would declare נידוי on you, because you are feeding the Jewish people קדשים outside the בית המקדש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next leniency of רבן גמליאל in the משנה, the whole roasted kid. It brings a story showing how strongly the Sages objected to this custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גדי מקולס is a goat roasted whole, with its legs and innards on its head, the way the קרבן פסח was roasted. Eating it on פסח night outside the בית המקדש looks like eating a קרבן פסח where it may not be eaten. The חכמים held back from punishing תודוס only because he was an important leader.

keyTerms.meaning: A young goat roasted whole, with its legs and innards on it, like the קרבן פסח
Established a custom; led people to do something
Sacred offerings eaten outside the Temple area

phrases.english: 'And we may make a whole roasted kid.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: one of רבן גמליאל's leniencies.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Todos (Theodosius) of Rome
led the people of Rome
to eat a whole roasted kid on Pesach nights.
They (the Sages) sent to him:
Were you not Todos,
we would decree a ban on you,
for you are feeding the Jewish people
sacred offerings outside (the Temple).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹשִׂין גְּדִי מְקוּלָּס. תַּנְיָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the incense discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating a whole roasted kid on Pesach night outside the Temple is strongly frowned upon, because it resembles eating קדשים outside.

steps.title: Were they really קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the ברייתא's wording. Could the Sages really mean that תודוס fed people actual קדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it was actual קדשים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the Sages' message in the ברייתא. Ordinary goats bought and roasted at home are obviously not sacred offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody in Rome had dedicated these goats as offerings, so they were plain חולין. Taking the message literally, as if it were real קדשים, makes no sense. That forces the גמרא to reread the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Could it enter your mind?'; signals that a reading is impossible

phrases.english: Can it enter your mind that it was sacred offerings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal wording of the ברייתא in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'קדשים בחוץ' in the Sages' message
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unconsecrated goats cannot be called קדשים, so the literal reading is impossible.

steps.title: Correcting the wording: something that looks like קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the message: he was feeding people something that resembles קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: something like קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The problem is not that the meat was sacred, but that it looked like a קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is about appearance. A whole roasted kid on פסח night looks just like a קרבן פסח, so people might think offerings can be eaten outside the בית המקדש. That is why the חכמים objected so strongly, even though the meat itself was ordinary.
steps.whatToRemember: Roasting a whole kid on פסח night is a problem because it looks like a קרבן פסח eaten outside the בית המקדש. The meat itself is not actually sacred.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
something similar to sacred offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The message seems to call ordinary goats real קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The meat only resembles קדשים, and that resemblance is the problem.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's three leniencies, starting with the cow's strap
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists three things that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid. The first: his cow went out on שבת with a strap between its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are three things that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits and the חכמים forbid. His cow goes out on שבת with a strap between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a list of three disputes. It opens with the first case, a cow wearing a strap between its horns on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal may not carry a burden (משאוי) on שבת, but it may wear things that count as ornaments or as part of its gear. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה sees the strap as decoration, so the cow may go out with it. The חכמים see it as a burden, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'; marks the start of a new משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens a new section built on a running dispute between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the חכמים. Its first case is about animals carrying things on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Three things
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya permits
and the Sages forbid:
His cow goes out (on Shabbat)
with the strap that is between its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מַתִּיר וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבן גמליאל's leniencies ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits a cow to go out on שבת with a strap between its horns, and the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: The second and third leniencies: combing an animal and grinding pepper
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the list of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's leniencies. He permits combing an animal on יום טוב and grinding pepper in its own mill.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may comb an animal on יום טוב. And one may grind peppers in their own mill.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list of three things that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits. After the cow with the strap, it adds combing an animal and grinding pepper in its special mill on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items are things that some might forbid on יום טוב. Fine combing might wound the animal, and grinding pepper in its usual mill looks like ordinary weekday work. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits both.

keyTerms.meaning: Combing an animal with a fine-toothed comb to remove dirt and ticks

phrases.english: And one may comb the animal on a Festival.
phrases.notes: This is the second of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's three leniencies.

phrases.english: And one may grind the peppers
in their own mill.
phrases.notes: This means the special pepper mill, even though using it looks like weekday work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list begun in step 15 with the second and third items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, one may comb an animal on יום טוב and grind pepper in its own mill.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and the Sages disagree about combing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids fine combing because it makes a wound, but he permits brushing. The חכמים forbid both combing and brushing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One may not comb an animal on יום טוב, because it makes a wound, but one may brush it. And the חכמים say: One may not comb, and one may not even brush.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents two other opinions about combing an animal. רבי יהודה allows only gentle brushing, while the חכמים forbid even that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's concern is חבורה, meaning drawing blood or bruising the animal, which is forbidden. He says a fine comb surely wounds, but a coarse brush does not. The חכמים are stricter and forbid brushing too.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound or bruise, such as causing blood to gather or come out
Brushing with a coarse, blunt-toothed comb
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not comb the animal on a Festival,
because it makes a wound,
phrases.notes: This gives the reason for his prohibition.

phrases.english: but one may brush.
phrases.notes: A blunt brush does not wound.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
One may not comb, nor even brush.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing opinions to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's leniency about combing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה forbids combing but permits brushing. The חכמים forbid both.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on combing an animal on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits combing. רבי יהודה permits brushing only. The חכמים forbid both.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר בן עזריה have only one cow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's phrase 'his cow,' since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was so rich that he tithed 13,000 calves every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא asks: Is this to say that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה had only one cow? But רב said (and some say רב יהודה said in the name of רב): רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would tithe 13,000 calves from his herds every single year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins discussing the משנה. It is puzzled that the משנה speaks of 'his cow,' as if he owned only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing 13,000 calves means he had about 130,000 new calves each year. So why would the משנה describe one particular cow as 'his'? The wording seems to clash with what we know about him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a surprised question)
And some say (introduces a different version of who said it)
Separates מעשר בהמה, the tithe of animals

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: GEMARA: Is that to say that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
had one cow?
But didn't Rav say,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
thirteen thousand calves

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְעַשַּׂר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would tithe
from his herds each and every year.
phrases.notes: A tithe is one out of ten, so his herds were enormous.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה חֲדָא פָּרָה הַוְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first item in the משנה (step 15) and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man who tithed 13,000 calves a year owned huge herds. Speaking of 'his cow' as if he had just one makes no sense.

steps.title: It was his neighbor's cow, called his because he did not protest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the cow belonged to his neighbor. Because he did not object to her conduct, the cow was called by his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The cow was not his. Rather, it was his neighbor's. Because he did not protest against her, it was called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The cow was really his neighbor's, but the משנה calls it his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor let her cow go out with the strap, which the חכמים forbid. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could have stopped her and did not. So the act was 'credited' to him, and the cow was called his as a criticism.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'his cow' in the משנה means he owned it. He is being blamed for failing to stop someone else's wrongdoing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that someone who can protest a wrongdoing and stays silent is held responsible, as if he did it himself.

phrases.english: It was taught: It was not his,
rather, it was his neighbor's,
and because he did not protest against her —
it was called by his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording based on a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His cow' means a cow he owned, which clashes with his great wealth.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'His cow' means a neighbor's cow that was attributed to him because he did not protest.

steps.title: Defining combing and brushing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about combing and brings a ברייתא that defines the difference. קירוד uses small teeth and makes a wound, while קרצוף uses large teeth and does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may comb an animal on יום טוב.' The Rabbis taught: What is combing and what is brushing? Combing is with small teeth and makes a wound. Brushing is with large teeth and does not make a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about combing. It brings a ברייתא to explain what the two terms mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is the comb's teeth. Small, fine teeth scratch the skin and wound it, while large, blunt teeth do not. This explains why רבי יהודה forbids one and permits the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Combing with a fine, small-toothed comb
Brushing with a coarse, large-toothed comb

phrases.english: 'And one may comb the animal on a Festival.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה to start discussing this line.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What is combing and what is brushing?
Combing — small teeth, and they make a wound,
brushing — large teeth, and they do not make a wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ קֵרוּד וְאֵיזֶהוּ קִרְצוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second item of the משנה and defines its key terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Combing uses a small-toothed comb and wounds. Brushing uses a large-toothed comb and does not wound.

steps.title: Three disputes, starting with רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה contains three opinions. רבי יהודה forbids דבר שאינו מתכוין, but he still permits brushing, because brushing never makes a wound and we do not make a גזירה on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three opinions on this matter. רבי יהודה holds that an unintended act is forbidden. Even so, he says combing uses small teeth and makes a wound, while brushing uses large teeth and does not. We do not forbid brushing because of combing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the reasoning behind each of the three opinions in the משנה. It starts with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a wound is a forbidden מלאכה. The person combing does not want to wound the animal, so the question is whether an unintended forbidden result is allowed. רבי יהודה says it is forbidden, so fine combing is not allowed. Brushing never wounds at all, and he does not worry that people will confuse the two, so brushing stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An act whose forbidden result is not intended
A wound or bruise (a forbidden מלאכה)
We make a protective rabbinic decree
Because of, out of concern for

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה permits brushing even though he forbids unintended acts. The reason is that brushing never makes a wound, so there is no unintended result to worry about in the first place.

phrases.english: And there are three disputes in the matter;
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
an unintentional act is forbidden.
phrases.notes: So combing that might wound is forbidden.

phrases.english: However: combing is with small teeth and makes a wound.
Brushing is with large teeth and does not make a wound.
And we do not decree against brushing because of combing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definitions from step 20 to explain the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: an unintended act is forbidden, so combing is forbidden. There is no גזירה on brushing, so brushing is permitted.

steps.title: The Sages forbid brushing as a protective decree
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that דבר שאינו מתכוין is forbidden. They go further and forbid brushing too, out of concern that people will come to comb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים also agree with רבי יהודה that an unintended act is forbidden. But they do forbid brushing because of combing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second opinion, that of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים share רבי יהודה's basic rule. The only difference is that they add a גזירה. Since brushing looks like combing, they forbid brushing as well.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis also hold like Rabbi Yehuda,
that an unintentional act is forbidden,
and we decree against brushing because of combing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second of the three opinions. It agrees with step 21 on the basic rule but adds a גזירה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: an unintended act is forbidden, and brushing is also forbidden because of combing.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follows רבי שמעון and permits both
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds like רבי שמעון that דבר שאינו מתכוין is permitted. Therefore both combing and brushing are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds like רבי שמעון, who said an unintended act is permitted. So both combing and brushing are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third opinion, the lenient view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the basic rule itself is different. Since the person does not intend to wound the animal, even a possible wound does not make the act forbidden. With no problem in combing, there is also no reason for any גזירה on brushing.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who permits unintended acts

steps.whatToRemember: The three opinions on combing: רבי יהודה forbids combing but permits brushing. The חכמים forbid both. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits both, following רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya holds like Rabbi Shimon,
who said: an unintentional act is permitted,
so both combing and brushing are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third opinion. It completes the explanation of the three opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: an unintended act is permitted, so combing and brushing are both allowed.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן (possibly in the name of שמואל) rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. His reason is that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן, in the name of שמואל, and some say רב נחמן said it on his own: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives a practical ruling on which opinion we follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who said this ruling: רב נחמן quoting שמואל, or רב נחמן alone. The reason given is that רבי שמעון has support from another תנא, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: an unintended forbidden result is permitted on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rava said Rav Nachman said Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן לְחוֹדֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Nachman said it by himself:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מוֹדֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: since Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the opinions to deciding the law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: an unintended act is permitted.

steps.title: רבא asks why not rule like רבי יהודה instead
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן's reason. If outside agreement decides the law, then רבי יהודה should win, since the חכמים agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Then let the master say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, since the חכמים agree with him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason רב נחמן gave for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reason was that someone agrees with רבי שמעון. But the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה on the basic rule, and they are the majority. So the same logic should point to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Then let the master say,
the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda,
since the Sages agree with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reason that 'רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Support from another opinion works even better for רבי יהודה, because the חכמים (the majority) agree with him on the basic rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן holds like רבי שמעון on his own reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he rules like רבי שמעון because he agrees with his logic. The agreement of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is only an extra support.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I myself hold like רבי שמעון. And in addition, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not based on counting who agrees with whom. רב נחמן is convinced by רבי שמעון's reasoning. The support from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is just an added point.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold, it is my opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: an unintended forbidden result is permitted. רב נחמן holds this on its own merits, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's agreement is only extra support.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I hold like Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד שֶׁהֲרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מוֹדֶה לוֹ.
phrases.english: and furthermore, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the reason: the ruling stands on its own logic, and the agreement is only extra support.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling depended entirely on which opinion has outside agreement.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן holds like רבי שמעון on the merits. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's agreement is only an added point.
